To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the vast majority of single-copy gene orthologs are resistant to horizontal gene transfer, even in groups subject to extensive gene transfer, and that (2) the resulting gene set can be used to reconstruct the organismal phylogenetic relationships in these groups, thereby establishing the foundation for understanding the evolutionary processes that shape genome content and organization.

the phylogeny of γ-Proteobacterial species is fully resolved by concatenating the protein sequences of 203 genes that are likely orthologous, and that the phylogenic relationships among the species are congruent with the phylogeny inferred from the concatenated sequences.

(1) the vast majority (203 of 206) of single-copy, likely orthologous gene families in the γ-proteobacteria yield phylogenetically congruent gene trees, and (2) the concatenated sequence of the congruent gene families yields a phylogenetic hypothesis that is fully resolved, well supported and consistent with the results of other studies.
